concerns: The headline LTP outcomes are established by the same llama3.3:70b judge that is used as the evaluation signal, and the reported human audit shows only moderate three-way agreement (kappa 0.699 overall, 0.578 on LoCoMo), so the claimed gains are not clearly corroborated by an independent measurement.

The component ablation on LTP Profiles 000-002 shows the full A-TMA configuration is not consistently best: removing Sentry yields the highest preferred accuracy and judge score, and removing QA labels raises conflict accuracy, which weakens the claim that the proposed components drive the reported improvements.

The LoCoMo generalization results are mixed and host-dependent, with A-Mem+A-TMA slightly lower on average F1 and BLEU-1 and several +A-TMA rows showing decreases, so the manuscript's own evidence does not support a clear promotion-worthy gain beyond the narrow LTP setting.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The manuscript presents a conceptually clear and practically impactful diagnostic formulation of state coordination in agent memory, backed by solid experimental controls, explicit architecture definitions, and honest reporting of mixed benchmark outcomes.

change. The central question is not only whether a fact can be remembered, but

The gains are host and metric dependent, with the clearest benefit when the host exposes enough
evidence but does not align bank state, retrieval state, and answer state by itself. Our contributions are:
• We formulate state changing long term memory as a three level problem over memory bank,
retrieval, and QA, which separates failures hidden by final answer accuracy.
• We identify ghost memory as a state coordination failure where old, current, and transition facts
remain mixed unless their roles are preserved and exposed.
• We introduce A-TMA, an overlay that maintains supersession structure, builds state aligned
evidence packets, and conditions QA on explicit evidence state labels.
• We construct LTP (LoCoMo Temporal Plus) as a conflict heavy benchmark and evaluate A-TMA
on LTP and LoCoMo, with host dependent gains on conflict aware and temporal queries.

evidence.excerpt:
We presented A-TMA, a tri level state aware framework for long term agent memory under changing
user states. A-TMA separates memory bank maintenance, state aware retrieval, and answer time
evidence resolution. This separation makes ghost memory measurable rather than treating it as a
single end to end QA failure.
The full LTP results support a bounded conclusion. A-TMA preserves strong A-Mem performance
and improves its conflict split. It gives larger gains for hosts whose retrieval and answer layers are
less state aligned. Full LoCoMo results are mixed by host and metric, so they support cautious
generalization rather than a universal improvement claim. Future agent memory evaluations should
report not only whether an answer is correct, but also which memory layer made the answer possible
or caused it to fail.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The headline LTP outcomes are established by the same llama3.3:70b judge that is used as the evaluation signal, and the reported human audit shows only moderate three-way agreement (kappa 0.699 overall, 0.578 on LoCoMo), so the claimed gains are not clearly corroborated by an independent measurement.

The component ablation on LTP Profiles 000-002 shows the full A-TMA configuration is not consistently best: removing Sentry yields the highest preferred accuracy and judge score, and removing QA labels raises conflict accuracy, which weakens the claim that the proposed components drive the reported improvements.

The LoCoMo generalization results are mixed and host-dependent, with A-Mem+A-TMA slightly lower on average F1 and BLEU-1 and several +A-TMA rows showing decreases, so the manuscript's own evidence does not support a clear promotion-worthy gain beyond the narrow LTP setting.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The manuscript reports a human audit of 100 judge outputs with 80% three-way agreement (kappa 0.699) and 93% binary agreement, but the LoCoMo subset shows only 72% three-way agreement (kappa 0.578), and the component ablation shows the full A-TMA configuration is not consistently best.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline LTP and LoCoMo outcomes are established by the offline llama3.3:70b answer judge, supplemented by lexical metrics such as F1 and BLEU-1.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The Sentry gate is trained with supervised topic and logic MSE losses, and the internal audit Judge is trained with SFT and GRPO using rule-based rewards on training subsets.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported findings closely reflect empirical results; authors explicitly acknowledge that gains are host- and metric-dependent and that LoCoMo demonstrates mixed generalization rather than uniform superiority.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The paper provides rigorous empirical validation across multiple host memory baselines on the 800-probe LTP dataset and the full 1,986 QA-pair LoCoMo benchmark, complete with ablations, metric definitions, and human-LLM judge reliability audits.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Objective lexical overlap metrics (F1, BLEU-1), strict QA target matches, and human audit verification (demonstrating 93% binary agreement with the evaluation judge) corroborate the reported trends.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline evaluation relies on objective exact/semantic accuracy splits (QA Acc, conflict/fact splits, BLEU-1, F1) alongside an independent offline Llama-3.3-70B judge.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The Sentry gate was trained on pairwise interaction MSE losses, while the internal audit Judge was fine-tuned via SFT and GRPO with rule-based rewards on training subsets.

primary.limitations: The study transparently documents boundaries: A-TMA cannot recover records never ingested by the host substrate, component ablations show modest variations on certain hosts, and generalization is host-dependent.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, specifying the multi-tier architecture comprising a Sentry proposal gate, a GRPO/SFT-trained audit Judge, query state view profiling, bounded retrieval re-ranking, and state-explicit QA serialization.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a conceptually clear and practically impactful diagnostic formulation of state coordination in agent memory, backed by solid experimental controls, explicit architecture definitions, and honest reporting of mixed benchmark outcomes.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript proposes A-TMA, a modular state-aware overlay for LLM agent long-term memory that decouples failures across bank maintenance, retrieval, and QA conditioning, evaluated on the newly constructed LTP benchmark and LoCoMo.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a conceptually clear and practically impactful diagnostic formulation of state coordination in agent memory, backed by solid experimental controls, explicit architecture definitions, and honest reporting of mixed benchmark outcomes.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The study transparently documents boundaries: A-TMA cannot recover records never ingested by the host substrate, component ablations show modest variations on certain hosts, and generalization is host-dependent.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
